channel.title: Diligent Dwarves
channel.description:
A channel dedicated to Craft and Creativity. 
Not just "Thinking outside the box", but ignoring there is a box.
Bringing nearly 50 years of crafting experience in; Film, TV, props & costumes as well as Space Exploration and Medieval Arms & Armour. 
Topics such as Armour, Spacesuits, Costume, Props and Effects. Join me in the discovery of Science, Technology, Techniques, and History.
Part of Global

videos.t: Casa Bardicci & Gaston House
videos.desc:
This is a portable camp made for use at a medieval event in North America called Pennsic. Pennsic war is run by a group called the Society for Creative Anachronism, or SCA and held every July/ August at Coopers Lake Campground in Slippery Rock Pennsylvania.  Pennsic was first held in 1972 https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsic_War
The camp, Casa Bardicci, was started by Bill Thorpe and James Lee Thorpe in the 1990's. Set 500 years ago, it’s a household of artists and musicians, inspired by the Medici family of the early 16th century, Casa Bardicci is headed by our patron, the mysterious Baron G

videos.t: Trans Am 1970
videos.desc:
Original Super 8 footage shot with a Canon 1014 electronic camera by Peg & Ralph Gilman.
Peg Gilman started in the SCCA - New England region in 1959. From the early 60's till the late 90's Peg was head of registration for many racing organizations, including; SCCA- NER, Lime Rock Park, IMSA, Cart. She is retired and now living in Palm Springs California.
Ralph Gilman also a member of the SCCA - NER and joined in 1957. Ralph spent many years in Flag & communications until starting his racing career late in life. After moving to Tucson Arizona, Ralph died in 1981.

videos.desc:
Hardened steel leg armor made by Robert MacPherson, with additional pieces by Jeff Wasson, (www.wassonartistry.com) decoration and assembly by Chris Gilman.

videos.t: Dave Beldon Ralph Gilman Spitfire at Bryer
How I made my Greenwich armour: Etching- Vinyl weeding
videos.desc:
I’m sure there are more experienced people doing tutorials of this work, but this application may be at a much finer scale than most vinyl cutting.
I have chosen to use a computer and a Zing-Orbit vinyl cutter to create the masking artwork, primarily because my illustration skills are not sufficient to get the correct artwork look, when drawing it directly onto the armour. Secondarily, I have a huge number of pieces to do, so this technique allows me create artwork for many elements, that can be used in multiple places.

videos.t: 1595 Greenwich Burgonet and Falling buff.
videos.desc:
This is one of the helmets for the 1595 Greenwich garniture. Known as an Burgonet, this helmet has three configurations;
1. Open faced with no bars
2. With only the 3-bar grill (installed here) 
3. With the falling buff (shown here)
 This type of helmet was used by a Lancer or Infantry Captain .

 See my other video of the other helmets for this garniture.
For more on Greenwich armours, check out this video with my friend Dr. Tobias Capwell: https://youtu.be/QKlUy9NOl_U?si=ABcuVhZiYl6Yrv46

videos.t: My friend trying out the upper part of the Greenwich armour.
videos.desc:
Late 16th C Greenwich armor made by Robert MacPherson, with additional pieces by Jeff Wasson, decoration and assembly by Chris Gilman. 
This is nearly an exact copy of a 1587 Greenwich armour that is in the Wallace Collection (London) and another armour in the Metropolitan Museum of Art (NYC). 
All hand formed 1050 spring steel, which has been heat treated polished, then heat blued, with 24 k gold plated etching.
 The armour worn here weighs 21.82kg / 48.1lbs each. 

Additional videos on this playlist:
https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL_HgI1vD_fO9gKlxJBZ9FTKTLkx4-2m30

For more on Greenw

videos.t: Hardened steel Greenwich Armet with Jousting Visor
videos.desc:
Hardened steel Greenwich Armet (Helmet) with jousting visor,  made by Robert MacPherson, &  Jeff Wasson, decoration and assembly by Chris Gilman. 
This one part of a nearly an exact copy of a 1587 Greenwich armour that is in the Wallace Collection (London) and another armour in the Metropolitan Museum of Art (NYC). 
This helmet is made from heat treated 1050 spring steel. The vibrant blue, is created using just heat. 300 c creates a deep blue oxide on the surface of the steel. The gold, is 24 k gold.
This helmet weighs 3.98kg / 8.77lbs
The gorget (throat protection) weighs: 1.23kg / 2.7lbs

Ad

videos.t: Greenwich Garniture: Armet with field visor & visor reinforce.
videos.desc: This is one of the helmets for the 1595 Greenwich garniture. Known as an armet, this helmet has two visors, one for field, one for jousting. This is the field visor, with an additional, removable reinforce. The helmet locks on to the gorget (throat protection) and freely rotates. I am moving my head as far as it goes, the helmet does not limit my range of motion.  See my other video of this helmet with the jousting visor.

videos.t: Making A Gauntlet - The Greenwich Armour Project
videos.desc:
Here is a longer more comprehensive video on how the gauntlets for the Greenwich armour were made. This includes the beginnings of the projects as well as the etching and assembly of the gauntlets.

A couple errors; I misspoke and said “Earl of Buckhurst”, I meant to say “Lord Buckhurst “
Also at 3:45, I wrongly attribute the gauntlet to the Clifford Armour, but it is in fact a gauntlet from the early 17th c armour of Henry Prince of Wales.
